from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "What is the fastest path between two points?",
            "A straight line is shortest, but is it fastest?",
            "Gravity accelerates objects differently on various curves.",
            "Let's compare a straight line and a steep curve.",
            "Surprisingly, the longer, steeper path wins the race."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Counter-Intuitive Race", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        point_a = Dot(self.grid["A2"], color="#FFFFFF")
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(point_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        point_b = Dot(self.grid["E5"], color="#FFFFFF")
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(point_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(point_a), Create(label_a), Create(point_b), Create(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Straight Track
        straight_track = Line(self.grid["A2"], self.grid["E5"], color="#00FF00")
        label_straight = Text("Shortest", font_size=16, color="#00FF00").next_to(straight_track, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(straight_track), FadeIn(label_straight))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Circular Track
        circular_track = ArcBetweenPoints(self.grid["A2"], self.grid["E5"], radius=4, color="#0000FF")
        
        # Steep Track (Cycloid-like shape using CubicBezier)
        # We want it to go down fast then move towards B
        start = self.grid["A2"]
        end = self.grid["E5"]
        # Control points to make it steep
        c1 = start + DOWN * 4
        c2 = end + LEFT * 2
        steep_track = CubicBezier(start, c1, c2, end, color="#FF0000")
        
        self.play(Create(circular_track), Create(steep_track))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Three Spheres
        sphere_straight = Dot(self.grid["A2"], color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.12)
        sphere_circular = Dot(self.grid["A2"], color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.12)
        sphere_steep = Dot(self.grid["A2"], color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.12)
        
        self.add(sphere_straight, sphere_circular, sphere_steep)
        
        # Race using ValueTracker for relative timing
        race_time = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Steep: 1.5s, Straight: 2.2s, Circular: 2.8s
        sphere_steep.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(steep_track.point_from_proportion(min(race_time.get_value() / 1.5, 1))))
        sphere_straight.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(straight_track.point_from_proportion(min(race_time.get_value() / 2.2, 1))))
        sphere_circular.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circular_track.point_from_proportion(min(race_time.get_value() / 2.8, 1))))
        
        self.play(race_time.animate.set_value(2.8), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        sphere_steep.clear_updaters()
        sphere_straight.clear_updaters()
        sphere_circular.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight winner
        winner_text = Text("Fastest Path", font_size=28, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(winner_text, "C4")
        
        highlight_rect = SurroundingRectangle(winner_text, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Indicate(sphere_steep, color="#FF0000", scale_factor=2.5))
        self.play(Flash(sphere_steep, color="#FF0000", line_length=0.3))
        self.play(Write(winner_text), Create(highlight_rect))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the specific lecture lines for Section 3
        title = "The Physics: Energy to Velocity"
        lines = [
            "In gravity, potential energy converts to kinetic energy.",
            "Velocity depends on the vertical distance fallen.",
            "This links depth directly to the speed of travel."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard
        COLOR_WIRE = "#888888"
        COLOR_BEAD = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_Y = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_V = "#00FFFF"
        
        # Grid positions: B2 (start) to E5 (end)
        start_pt = self.grid["B2"]
        end_pt = self.grid["E5"]
        # Control points for a steep-then-curved descent
        cp1 = self.grid["D2"]
        cp2 = self.grid["E3"]
        wire = CubicBezier(start_pt, cp1, cp2, end_pt, color=COLOR_WIRE)
        
        # Pre-sample points for performance optimization
        NUM_SAMPLES = 100
        samples = [wire.point_from_proportion(i/(NUM_SAMPLES-1)) for i in range(NUM_SAMPLES)]
        
        def get_pos(alpha_val):
            alpha_val = np.clip(alpha_val, 0, 1)
            idx = alpha_val * (NUM_SAMPLES - 1)
            i0 = int(idx)
            i1 = min(i0 + 1, NUM_SAMPLES - 1)
            frac = idx - i0
            return (1-frac)*samples[i0] + frac*samples[i1]

        # --- Visual Objects ---
        bead = Dot(color=COLOR_BEAD, radius=0.1)
        bead.move_to(start_pt)
        
        y_bar = Line(start_pt, start_pt, color=COLOR_Y, stroke_width=4)
        y_label = MathTex("y", color=COLOR_Y, font_size=24)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"v = \sqrt{2gy}", color=COLOR_V, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A5")
        
        v_arrow = Arrow(start_pt, start_pt + RIGHT*0.1, color=COLOR_V, buff=0, 
                        stroke_width=3, max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.3)
        v_arrow.set_opacity(0)
        
        alpha = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_elements(m):
            a = alpha.get_value()
            p = get_pos(a)
            bead.move_to(p)
            
            # Height indicator 'y'
            y_top = np.array([p[0], start_pt[1], 0])
            y_bar.put_start_and_end_on(y_top, p)
            # Position label to the left of the bar's midpoint
            y_label.move_to(y_top + DOWN * (start_pt[1] - p[1]) / 2 + LEFT * 0.3)
            
            # Velocity vector 'v'
            if a > 0.01:
                p_prev = get_pos(a - 0.01)
                dir_vec = p - p_prev
                dist = np.linalg.norm(dir_vec)
                if dist > 1e-6:
                    unit_v = dir_vec / dist
                    y_drop = max(0, start_pt[1] - p[1])
                    # Magnitude follows physics v ~ sqrt(y)
                    v_mag = np.sqrt(y_drop) * 1.5
                    v_arrow.put_start_and_end_on(p, p + unit_v * v_mag)
                    v_arrow.set_opacity(1)
            else:
                v_arrow.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "In gravity, potential energy converts to kinetic energy."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(wire), FadeIn(bead), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Velocity depends on the vertical distance fallen."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_Y)
        
        bead.add_updater(update_elements)
        self.add(y_bar, y_label)
        
        # Initial drop to introduce 'y'
        self.play(alpha.animate.set_value(0.2), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "This links depth directly to the speed of travel."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_V)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(formula), FadeIn(v_arrow), run_time=0.8)
        
        # Full descent along the curve
        self.play(alpha.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        bead.clear_updaters()

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Light Analogy Solution"
        lines = [
            "Imagine gravity as layers of increasing light speed.",
            "Each layer bends the path slightly to save time.",
            "Snell’s Law dictates the exact ratio of the curve.",
            "The math reveals a specific differential equation.",
            "This equation defines our optimal, fastest path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create thin horizontal layers with increasing brightness
        num_layers = 10
        layers = VGroup()
        top_left = self.grid["A1"]
        bottom_right = self.grid["F6"]
        # Use a slightly wider area for the layers to cover the right side
        width = 6.0 
        height_total = 5.0
        layer_height = height_total / num_layers
        
        for i in range(num_layers):
            # Calculate color brightness (0.1 to 0.7)
            alpha = 0.1 + (i / num_layers) * 0.6
            layer_color = interpolate_color(DARK_GRAY, BLUE_E, alpha)
            layer = Rectangle(
                width=width, 
                height=layer_height, 
                fill_color=layer_color, 
                fill_opacity=0.3, 
                stroke_width=0.5,
                stroke_color=GRAY
            )
            # Position layer - start from top row A
            y_pos = 2.2 - (i * layer_height)
            layer.move_to([3.0, y_pos, 0])
            layers.add(layer)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(layers, lag_ratio=0.1), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Trace a light ray (#FFFF00) bending through each layer
        ray_points = []
        # Start at top center of grid area
        start_point = self.grid["A2"] + LEFT * 0.5 + UP * 0.5
        ray_points.append(start_point)
        
        current_p = start_point
        # Bending logic: angle relative to vertical changes
        for i in range(num_layers):
            angle = np.deg2rad(-20 - (i * 6)) 
            step = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * 0.6
            current_p = current_p + step
            ray_points.append(current_p)
            
        ray = VMobject(color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        ray.set_points_as_corners(ray_points)
        
        self.play(Create(ray), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Smooth the jagged ray into a continuous curve
        smooth_ray = VMobject(color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        smooth_ray.set_points_smoothly(ray_points)
        
        snells_law = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin\theta}{v} = k", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(snells_law, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(ray, smooth_ray),
            Write(snells_law)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show substitution: v = sqrt(y)
        v_sub = MathTex(r"v = \sqrt{2gy}", font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(v_sub, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        final_formula_text = r"\frac{\sin\theta}{\sqrt{y}} = k"
        final_eq = MathTex(final_formula_text, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(final_eq, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(v_sub, shift=DOWN))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            Transform(snells_law, final_eq),
            FadeOut(v_sub)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight the final equation in cyan
        highlight_eq = MathTex(final_formula_text, color="#00FFFF", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(highlight_eq, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(highlight_eq, color="#00FFFF", buff=0.15)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(snells_law, highlight_eq),
            Create(rect)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Transition out
        self.play(
            *[FadeOut(m) for m in [layers, ray, snells_law, rect]]
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The solution to this problem is the cycloid.",
            "A cycloid is traced by a point on a rolling circle.",
            "It provides the perfect balance of speed and distance.",
            "It starts steeply to gain rapid initial velocity.",
            "Then, it curves efficiently toward the finish point."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Revealing the Cycloid", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        CYCLOID_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        CIRCLE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        TEXT_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Horizontal line for rolling
        ground_line = Line(
            start=self.grid["C1"] + LEFT * 0.5,
            end=self.grid["C6"] + RIGHT * 0.5,
            color=GRAY
        )
        self.play(Create(ground_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT)

        # Rolling Circle setup
        radius = 0.5
        circle = Circle(radius=radius, color=CIRCLE_COLOR)
        # Starting position at C1, sitting on the line
        start_center = self.grid["C1"] + UP * radius
        circle.move_to(start_center)
        
        # Red dot on circumference (starts at bottom)
        dot = Dot(color=CYCLOID_COLOR)
        dot.move_to(start_center + DOWN * radius)
        
        # Tracker for angle theta
        theta = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Updaters
        def update_circle(c):
            t = theta.get_value()
            c.move_to(start_center + RIGHT * radius * t)
            c.set_angle(-t)

        def update_dot(d):
            t = theta.get_value()
            center = start_center + RIGHT * radius * t
            # Point on rim: x = R(t - sin t), y = R(1 - cos t) relative to start
            # relative to current center: x_rel = -R*sin(t), y_rel = -R*cos(t)
            d.move_to(center + np.array([-radius * np.sin(t), -radius * np.cos(t), 0]))

        circle.add_updater(update_circle)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)
        
        # Path tracing
        path = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color=CYCLOID_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.add(circle, dot, path)
        # Roll circle for one full revolution (2*pi)
        self.play(theta.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Finalize the path as a static object for manipulation
        # Points for a cycloid: x = r(t-sin t), y = r(1-cos t) relative to start position (bottom)
        start_floor = self.grid["C1"]
        cycloid_points = [
            start_floor + np.array([radius * (t - np.sin(t)), radius * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0])
            for t in np.linspace(0, 2 * PI, 50)
        ]
        static_cycloid = VMobject(color=CYCLOID_COLOR).set_points_as_corners(cycloid_points)
        
        # Remove dynamic objects, add static path
        circle.remove_updater(update_circle)
        dot.remove_updater(update_dot)
        self.remove(circle, dot, path)
        self.add(static_cycloid)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Rotate/Flip the cycloid 180 degrees to face downwards (Inverted Cycloid)
        # Rotate around its start point C1 (ground level)
        pivot = self.grid["C1"]
        self.play(
            Rotate(static_cycloid, angle=PI, axis=RIGHT, about_point=pivot),
            ground_line.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Label the curve
        label = Text("The Cycloid", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "E4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.play(Indicate(static_cycloid, color=CYCLOID_COLOR))
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture lines for Section 6
        lecture_lines = [
            "The cycloid also has the unique tautochrone property.",
            "Objects released from anywhere reach the bottom simultaneously.",
            "This \"equal time\" property defines this remarkable curve."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout("The Tautochrone Property & Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Constants for the cycloid fitting the grid
        # Grid range: Horizontal 0.5 to 5.5, Vertical 2.2 to -2.8
        a = 0.8
        h_offset = 3.0
        v_offset = 1.0

        def cycloid_func(theta):
            # Parametric equation shifted to fit the right-side grid
            # x(theta) = a(theta - sin(theta)), y(theta) = -a(1 - cos(theta))
            # Centered horizontally around theta=pi
            x = h_offset + a * (theta - np.pi)
            y = v_offset - a * (1 - np.cos(theta))
            return np.array([x, y, 0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1 color change
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_B)
        
        # Create cycloid curve
        # Range 0 to 2*pi covers one full arch. Bottom valley is at pi.
        cycloid_curve = ParametricFunction(
            cycloid_func,
            t_range=[0, 2 * np.pi],
            color=BLUE_B
        )
        
        # Place spheres at different heights (different starting thetas)
        theta1_start = 0.15 * np.pi
        theta2_start = 0.65 * np.pi
        
        sphere1 = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.15)
        sphere2 = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.15)
        
        sphere1.move_to(cycloid_func(theta1_start))
        sphere2.move_to(cycloid_func(theta2_start))
        
        self.play(Create(cycloid_curve), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere1), FadeIn(sphere2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2 color change
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_A)
        
        # ValueTracker for motion progress p (0 to 1)
        # p=0 is start, p=1 is reaching the bottom (theta = pi)
        progress = ValueTracker(0)

        def get_theta_at_time(theta_start, p):
            # Tautochrone physics logic: cos(theta/2) = cos(theta_start/2) * cos(pi/2 * p)
            # This ensures both reach theta=pi when p=1 regardless of theta_start.
            val = np.cos(theta_start / 2) * np.cos(np.pi / 2 * p)
            return 2 * np.arccos(np.clip(val, -1, 1))

        # Add updaters for the spheres to move along the curve
        sphere1.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(cycloid_func(get_theta_at_time(theta1_start, progress.get_value()))))
        sphere2.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(cycloid_func(get_theta_at_time(theta2_start, progress.get_value()))))

        # Run the animation to the bottom
        self.play(progress.animate.set_value(1), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3 color change
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN_A)
        
        # Highlight simultaneous arrival at the bottom (theta = pi)
        arrival_point = cycloid_func(np.pi)
        success_flash = Flash(arrival_point, color=GREEN_A, flash_radius=0.5)
        
        self.play(success_flash)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Clear updaters for cleanup
        sphere1.clear_updaters()
        sphere2.clear_updaters()

outline.topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Path of Fastest Descent
outline.target_audience: University undergraduates in Physics/Math or advanced High School students

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Race
sections.content: Introduce the paradox of the 'shortest path' versus the 'fastest path'. Most people assume a straight line is the fastest, but gravity changes the rules. We establish the goal: finding the curve between two points (A and B) that minimizes travel time for a sliding object.
sections.example: An animation showing three tracks: a straight line, a circular arc, and a steep curve. Three identical marbles are released simultaneously; the marble on the steep curve wins, defying the 'straight line' intuition.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Snell's Law and Fermat's Principle
sections.content: Before solving the mechanics, we look at optics. Fermat's Principle states light always takes the path of least time. Snell's Law (sinθ/v = constant) describes how light bends when its speed changes. This is the crucial 'cheat code' for the Brachistochrone problem.
sections.example: A visual of a laser beam bending as it moves from air into water. A side-by-side comparison shows that as velocity (v) increases in a medium, the angle of the path (θ) must also increase to maintain the ratio.

sections.title: The Physics: Energy to Velocity
sections.content: Transition back to gravity. Introduce the Law of Conservation of Energy (mgh = 1/2 mv²). This establishes that the speed (v) of the falling object is proportional to the square root of its vertical drop (y). This links the 'speed' in our optics analogy to the 'depth' of the curve.
sections.example: A bead sliding down a wire with a dynamic speed gauge. As the bead drops lower (increasing y), the gauge shows the velocity (v) increasing at a rate of v = sqrt(2gy).

sections.title: The Light Analogy Solution
sections.content: The core logic: Imagine the path is made of infinite thin layers of glass. As the object falls, it enters layers where it can move faster. Using Snell's Law, we find the mathematical relationship: sinθ / sqrt(y) = constant. This differential equation describes the 'shape' of the fastest path.
sections.example: An animation transforming the sliding bead into a ray of light passing through hundreds of horizontal layers, each slightly 'faster' than the one above, causing the ray to curve smoothly downward and then back up.

sections.title: Revealing the Cycloid
sections.content: Define the resulting curve: The Cycloid. A cycloid is the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling circle. This shape perfectly balances the need for a steep initial drop (to gain speed quickly) with a direct path toward the finish.
sections.example: A bicycle wheel rolling along a flat line with a glowing LED on the rim. As the wheel moves, the LED traces a 'hump' shape in the air. We flip this shape upside down to reveal the Brachistochrone track.

sections.title: The Tautochrone Property & Application
sections.content: Conclude with a unique property of the cycloid: the Tautochrone property. No matter where you release the object on a cycloid curve, it will reach the bottom in the exact same amount of time.
sections.example: Two skateboarders on a giant cycloid-shaped half-pipe. One starts near the bottom, the other at the very top. They are released at the same time and collide perfectly at the lowest point, demonstrating the 'equal time' property.
